NAME:
   Cameradar - Scan targets for RTSP streams

USAGE:
   Cameradar [global options] [command [command options]]

VERSION:
   dev

COMMANDS:
   version  Print version information
   help, h  Shows a list of commands or help for one command

GLOBAL OPTIONS:
   --targets string, -t string [ --targets string, -t string ]  The targets on which to scan for open RTSP streams in a network range format [$TARGETS]
   --ports string, -p string [ --ports string, -p string ]      The ports on which to search for RTSP streams (default: "554", "5554", "8554", "http", "322", "8322") [$PORTS]
   --custom-routes string, -r string                            The path on which to load a custom routes dictionary [$CUSTOM_ROUTES]
   --custom-credentials string, -c string                       The path on which to load a custom credentials JSON dictionary [$CUSTOM_CREDENTIALS]
   --scanner string                                             Discovery scanner backend: nmap or masscan (default: "nmap") [$SCANNER]
   --scan-speed int, -s int                                     The nmap speed preset to use for scanning (lower is stealthier) (default: 4) [$SCAN_SPEED]
   --attack-interval duration, -I duration                      The interval between each attack (i.e: 2000ms, higher is stealthier) (default: 0s) [$ATTACK_INTERVAL]
   --timeout duration, -T duration                              The timeout to use for attack attempts (i.e: 2000ms) (default: 2s) [$TIMEOUT]
   --framecheck                                                 When DESCRIBE returns 200 OK, require a frame probe check before accepting routes or credentials (slower) [$FRAMECHECK]
   --skip-scan                                                  Skip discovery and treat every target and port as an RTSP stream [$SKIP_SCAN]
   --debug, -d                                                  Enable debug logs [$DEBUG]
   --ui string                                                  UI mode: auto, tui, or plain (default: "auto") [$UI]
   --output string                                              Write discovered streams to an M3U file at the given path [$OUTPUT]
   --help, -h                                                   show help
   --version, -v                                                print the version

NAME:
   Cameradar version - Print version information

USAGE:
   Cameradar version [options]

OPTIONS:
   --help, -h  show help

GLOBAL OPTIONS:
   --targets string, -t string [ --targets string, -t string ]  The targets on which to scan for open RTSP streams in a network range format [$TARGETS]

   --custom-credentials string, -c string                       The path on which to load a custom credentials JSON dictionary [$CUSTOM_CREDENTIALS]
   --scanner string                                             Discovery scanner backend: nmap or masscan (default: "nmap") [$SCANNER]
   --scan-speed int, -s int                                     The nmap speed preset to use for scanning (lower is stealthier) (default: 4) [$SCAN_SPEED]
   --attack-interval duration, -I duration                      The interval between each attack (i.e: 2000ms, higher is stealthier) (default: 0s) [$ATTACK_INTERVAL]
   --timeout duration, -T duration                              The timeout to use for attack attempts (i.e: 2000ms) (default: 2s) [$TIMEOUT]
   --framecheck                                                 When DESCRIBE returns 200 OK, require a frame probe check before accepting routes or credentials (slower) [$FRAMECHECK]
